notes.meaning: The people of God repeat their thanks because their gratitude is deep and sincere. God's name means His personal presence and power, showing He is not far off or uncaring. The wondrous things He has done for His people prove that He is right beside them, ready to help.

God speaks directly here to comfort His people. He has a set, appointed time to step in and set things right. Human judges can be unfair or hasty, but the Lord promises that His justice will be completely fair and will arrive right on schedule.

When human society falls into chaos and war, the whole earth seems to shake and melt away in fear. Yet God is the one who set the pillars of creation in place and keeps them steady. Even in the worst times of turmoil, the world will not collapse, because God upholds it.

The Lord warns the proud and wicked to stop boasting about their power. In the Bible, an animal's horn is a picture of strength and honor. Lifting up one's horn means acting arrogant and trying to dominate others.

Sinners are warned not to defy God or speak with stubborn pride. The picture of an outstretched neck comes from an untamed ox refusing to lower its head for the yoke. Defying the God of heaven is foolish, because no human strength can stand against Him.

True honor and promotion do not come from human effort, luck, or any direction on earth. People often look east, west, and across the desert searching for power and success on their own. Yet no earthly corner holds the key to true advancement.

God alone sits as the true Judge of all rulers and nations. He decides who is brought down from power and who is raised up. World leaders are not in ultimate control; they only hold authority because the Lord places it in their hands.

The Lord holds a cup of judgment, pictured as foaming wine made potent with strong spices. He pours out this punishment on unrepentant sinners, who must drink every single drop down to the bitter dregs at the bottom. This shows that His justice against evil is thorough and cannot be avoided.

While the wicked face judgment, the psalmist resolves to praise God without end. He honors the Lord as the God of Jacob, the faithful covenant God who rescues His people from trouble. God's righteous rule gives His followers lasting reason to rejoice and sing.

The psalm closes with God speaking once again to promise that evil will not prevail. He will strip away the power, pride, and authority of the wicked. At the same time, He will lift up the strength and honor of those who walk faithfully with Him.
